topics.hook: Why does Pakistan have 5 of the world's 14 highest mountains?
facts: Only 14 mountains on Earth are taller than 8,000 metres.
5 of them are in Pakistan: K2 (8,611 m), Nanga Parbat (8,126 m), Gasherbrum I (8,080 m), Broad Peak (8,051 m) and Gasherbrum II (8,035 m).
K2 is the second-highest mountain in the world, on the Pakistan-China border in the Karakoram range.
K2, Broad Peak and both Gasherbrums stand within a few dozen kilometres of each other around the Baltoro Glacier.
Nanga Parbat is the western anchor of the Himalayas.
These ranges exist because the Indian plate is still pushing north into Asia.

topics.hook: Why is there a piece of Russia in the middle of the EU?
facts: Kaliningrad is a part of Russia on the Baltic Sea, squeezed between Poland and Lithuania.
It has no land connection to the rest of Russia.
The city was the German city of Königsberg until 1945.
After World War II the Soviet Union took the area.
When the Soviet Union broke up in 1991, Lithuania and Belarus became independent and Kaliningrad was cut off from Russia.
Its port on the Baltic usually stays ice-free in winter.

topics.hook: Pakistan bought a city from Oman. Here's how.
facts: Gwadar, on Pakistan's coast, was ruled by Oman for about 175 years.
In 1783 the Khan of Kalat granted Gwadar to a ruler of Muscat (Oman).
Pakistan bought Gwadar from the Sultan of Muscat and Oman, Said bin Taimur.
Pakistan took over Gwadar on 8 September 1958.
The price was about 5.5 billion rupees, and the Aga Khan paid most of it.
Today Gwadar is a deep-sea port city on the Arabian Sea.

topics.hook: Europe and Africa are only 13 km apart.
facts: The Strait of Gibraltar is only 13 km wide at its narrowest point.
The narrowest point is between Point Marroquí in Spain and Point Cires in Morocco.
It is the only natural link between the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea.
Gibraltar, at its northern side, is a British overseas territory.
Ceuta, on the African side, is a Spanish city.

topics.hook: This country is completely inside another country.
facts: Lesotho is completely surrounded by South Africa.
It is one of only three countries entirely surrounded by a single other country, with San Marino and Vatican City.
Lesotho's lowest point is 1,400 metres above sea level, the highest low point of any country.
The whole country lies above 1,000 metres, so it is called the Kingdom in the Sky.
Its capital is Maseru.

topics.hook: Ships go EAST to reach the Pacific in Panama.
facts: The Panama Canal is about 82 km long and opened in 1914.
It connects the Atlantic (Caribbean) to the Pacific Ocean.
Because Panama bends, the canal's Pacific end at Panama City is east of its Atlantic end at Colón.
Locks lift ships about 26 metres up to Gatun Lake and back down.
Before the canal, ships sailed around South America.

topics.hook: This 65 km gap might be the most dangerous place in Europe.
facts: The Suwałki Gap is a stretch of land about 65 km wide along the Poland-Lithuania border.
It separates Russia's Kaliningrad from Belarus, Russia's ally.
It is the only land link between the Baltic states (Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia) and the rest of NATO.
If it were ever closed, the Baltic states would be cut off by land.

topics.hook: The highest paved border crossing on Earth is in Pakistan.
facts: Khunjerab Pass sits at 4,693 metres above sea level.
It is the highest paved international border crossing in the world.
It links Pakistan's Gilgit-Baltistan with China's Xinjiang.
It is the highest point on the Karakoram Highway.
The Karakoram Highway runs about 1,300 km from Hasan Abdal in Pakistan to Kashgar in China.

topics.hook: Why does Namibia have this long arm?
facts: The Caprivi Strip is a narrow arm of Namibia stretching east between Angola, Zambia and Botswana.
Its width varies from about 32 km to 105 km.
Germany got it in 1890 through the Heligoland-Zanzibar Treaty with Britain, negotiated by Chancellor Leo von Caprivi.
Germany wanted access to the Zambezi River as a route to the east coast of Africa.
But the Zambezi was not navigable to the ocean: Victoria Falls lies about 65 km east of the strip.
At its eastern tip the strip comes within 150 metres of Zimbabwe.

topics.hook: China is huge. So why does it have just ONE time zone?
facts: China is about as wide as five time zones.
But since 1949 the whole country uses a single time: Beijing time, UTC+8.
In the far west, in places like Kashgar, the sun can rise as late as about 10 a.m. in winter.
Many people in Xinjiang also use an unofficial local time two hours behind Beijing.

topics.hook: This part of Angola isn't connected to Angola.
facts: Cabinda is a province of Angola that is not connected to the rest of Angola.
A narrow strip of the Democratic Republic of the Congo along the Congo River separates them.
That strip gives the DR Congo its short coastline on the Atlantic.
A big part of Angola's oil comes from Cabinda and its offshore waters.

topics.hook: Pakistan's lifeline starts in Tibet.
facts: The Indus River is about 3,180 km long.
It starts in Tibet near Mount Kailash and Lake Manasarovar.
It flows through Ladakh and Gilgit-Baltistan, then the whole length of Pakistan.
It reaches the Arabian Sea south-east of Karachi.
Most of Pakistan's farms depend on water from the Indus and its rivers.
The Indus Valley Civilisation, one of the world's oldest, grew along it.

topics.hook: This was once the 4th largest lake on Earth. Now look at it.
facts: In 1960 the Aral Sea was the fourth-largest inland body of water in the world.
In the early 1960s the Soviet Union diverted its two rivers, the Amu Darya and Syr Darya.
The water went to irrigate cotton fields in the desert.
By 2007 the Aral Sea had shrunk to about 10% of its original size.
Former fishing ports like Moynaq are now far from the water.

topics.hook: This country is just a river.
facts: The Gambia is the smallest country on mainland Africa.
It is surrounded by Senegal on every side except its short Atlantic coast.
The country follows the Gambia River inland.
It is less than 50 km wide.
Its capital is Banjul, at the mouth of the river.

topics.hook: A quarter of the world's sea oil passes through this gap.
facts: The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman.
It is about 54 km wide at its narrowest.
In 2025 an average of about 20 million barrels of oil a day passed through it.
That is about a quarter of all oil traded by sea.
Iran is on the north side; on the south side is Musandam, a part of Oman cut off from the rest of Oman by the UAE.

topics.hook: Why is Chile so long and thin?
facts: Chile is about 4,300 km long from north to south.
On average it is less than 180 km wide.
The Andes mountains form its eastern border with Argentina and Bolivia.
The Pacific Ocean is on its western side.
In the north is the Atacama, one of the driest deserts on Earth.

topics.hook: This part of Azerbaijan doesn't touch Azerbaijan.
facts: Nakhchivan is an exclave of Azerbaijan.
Armenia lies between Nakhchivan and the main part of Azerbaijan.
Nakhchivan borders Armenia, Iran and Turkey.
Its border with Turkey is very short.

topics.hook: The world's biggest lake is called a sea.
facts: The Caspian Sea is the largest lake on Earth by area, about 371,000 square km.
Its surface is about 28 metres below sea level.
Five countries border it: Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan.
It has no natural connection to the ocean.
Its water is salty, but less salty than the ocean.

topics.hook: No country wants this land. Here's why.
facts: Bir Tawil is about 2,060 square km of desert between Egypt and Sudan.
No country claims it.
An 1899 border followed a straight line along the 22nd parallel; a 1902 border was drawn differently.
Egypt uses the 1899 line, which gives the bigger Halaib Triangle to Egypt and Bir Tawil to Sudan.
Sudan uses the 1902 line, which gives Halaib to Sudan and Bir Tawil to Egypt.
So both claim Halaib, which has a coast on the Red Sea, and neither claims Bir Tawil.

topics.hook: This one lake holds about a fifth of Earth's lake and river water.
facts: Lake Baikal in Siberia is the deepest lake in the world, at about 1,642 metres.
It is also the oldest known lake, about 25 million years old.
It holds roughly a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water.
Over 300 rivers flow into it, but only one, the Angara, flows out.

topics.hook: This country's capital is on an island closer to another country.
facts: Equatorial Guinea's capital, Malabo, is on Bioko island, not on the mainland.
Bioko is much closer to Cameroon than to the country's own mainland, Río Muni.
Equatorial Guinea is the only country in Africa with Spanish as an official language.
It was a Spanish colony until 1968.

topics.hook: Russia has 11 time zones.
facts: Russia is the largest country in the world.
It has 11 time zones, from Kaliningrad in the west to Kamchatka in the east.
When it is 9 a.m. in Kaliningrad, it is already 7 p.m. in Kamchatka.
It is so wide it borders both the Baltic Sea and the Pacific Ocean.

topics.hook: Brazil touches almost every country in South America.
facts: Brazil borders 10 countries.
In South America, only Chile and Ecuador do not border Brazil.
One of its neighbours is France, through French Guiana.
Brazil covers almost half of South America.

topics.hook: Why does the USA have a bump on its straight border?
facts: The Northwest Angle in Minnesota is the only part of the contiguous United States north of the 49th parallel.
It sits on Lake of the Woods.
By land it can only be reached by driving through Canada.
It exists because the 1783 Treaty of Paris used an inaccurate map of the area's lakes and rivers.

topics.hook: Indonesia is wider than the United States.
facts: Indonesia is made of more than 17,000 islands.
From west to east it stretches more than 5,000 km.
That is wider than the mainland United States from coast to coast.
Its capital Jakarta is on the island of Java, one of the most crowded islands on Earth.

topics.hook: The USA bought Alaska for about 2 cents an acre.
facts: In 1867 the United States bought Alaska from Russia.
The price was 7.2 million dollars, about 2 cents an acre.
Critics called it Seward's Folly, after the Secretary of State who arranged it.
Gold and later oil were found in Alaska.
Across the Bering Strait, Alaska is only about 82 km from Russia.

topics.hook: Australia is wider than the Moon.
facts: Australia is about 4,000 km wide from west to east.
The Moon is about 3,474 km across.
So Australia is wider than the Moon.
Most Australians live near the coast, especially in the south-east.

topics.hook: The world's longest border is between two friends.
facts: The border between Canada and the United States is about 8,891 km long, the longest international border in the world.
It includes the border between Alaska and Canada.
A long section in the west follows the 49th parallel in a straight line.
It is often called the world's longest undefended border.

topics.hook: The roughest sea on Earth sits between South America and Antarctica.
facts: The Drake Passage is about 800 km wide, between Cape Horn and the South Shetland Islands of Antarctica.
It is known as one of the roughest stretches of sea in the world.
There is no land all the way around the Earth at this latitude, so winds and currents build up.
The Antarctic Circumpolar Current flows through it.

topics.hook: One city, two continents.
facts: Istanbul sits on both sides of the Bosphorus strait.
One side of the city is in Europe and the other is in Asia.
The Bosphorus is about 31 km long and only about 700 metres wide at its narrowest.
It connects the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara and on to the Mediterranean.
